title: Spectral Sensitivity of Directed Weighted Networks: Why Weakening Edges May Trigger Synchronization
summary: Synchronization in dynamical systems on directed weighted networks is often associated with stronger coupling and denser interactions. This paper shows that the opposite can also occur: weakening selected edges may increase the generalized algebraic connectivity, denoted by $κ$, and in some nonlinear systems this spectral improvement is accompanied by a transition from nonsynchronization to synchronization.
